name: Index dispersion trading
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Earning the Implied Correlation Premium
caseLead: Index dispersion trading seeks to earn the difference between implied correlation in index options and the lower correlation often realised between individual stocks. Index protection is often in strong demand from institutional investors, while company-specific earnings and sector developments can keep realised stock correlations below the level priced into index options.
caseRest: A sharp rise in stock correlations during an equity sell-off can make index options more expensive relative to the individual-stock options held as hedges. The strategy is short index volatility, so it loses in these episodes while the stock options it holds gain too little to offset the loss. Rehyn estimates that losses can build within days, so the gradual gains from many quiet months can be reversed in a single episode.
figNote: Each card shows the largest one-day fall in the S&P 500 during the episode. Dispersion trades tend to lose when the index falls sharply because stocks then move together, and to gain when large single-stock moves are not matched by the index.

events.title: US credit downgrade pushes stocks together
events.text: Standard and Poor's downgraded the US credit rating on 5 August 2011, and the S&P 500 fell about 6.7% on 8 August as stocks fell together. The strategy lost because index volatility rose by more than the volatility of individual stocks.

events.title: Covid turns into a global funding crisis
events.text: The March 2020 sell-off turned a health emergency into a global rush for cash, and the S&P 500 fell about 12% on 16 March. The strategy lost because almost all stocks fell together, so index volatility rose faster than the volatility of individual stocks.

events.title: Retail trading drives extreme single-stock moves
events.text: Retail buying of GameStop and other heavily shorted stocks produced extreme moves in individual shares in January 2021, while the S&P 500 fell about 2.6% on 27 January. The strategy gained because the volatility of individual stocks rose by more than index volatility.

events.title: Ukraine war splits stocks by sector
events.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 lifted energy shares while technology shares fell, and the S&P 500 fell about 3% on 7 March. Results were mixed because sector differences supported single-stock volatility while the falling market also raised correlation.

events.title: DeepSeek model hits chip stocks, not the index
events.text: The release of China's DeepSeek artificial intelligence model in January 2025 cut Nvidia's share price by about 17% on 27 January, while the S&P 500 fell about 1.5%. The strategy gained because the volatility of individual stocks rose while index volatility rose by less.

events.title: US tariffs push stocks together
events.text: The April 2025 announcement of sweeping US tariffs led the S&P 500 to fall about 6% on 4 April, as most sectors fell together. The strategy lost because correlation rose sharply and index volatility increased by more than the volatility of individual stocks.

instrument: S&P 500 index options and options on its 30 largest stocks; about two months to expiry; positions held two to six weeks
rules: Index straddles sold and single-stock straddles bought in vega-matched proportions when implied correlation exceeds realised correlation; stocks chosen across sectors; exposure reduced before earnings dates
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads on index and stock options and commissions deducted at each rebalance
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from correlation premium to vega balance

legs.purpose: Earns the premium priced into index volatility
Gains when stocks move independently of one another
Limits losses when stocks fall together
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: Implied correlation at least 5 points above realised correlation over three months
size: Index and stock volatility exposures matched; set to an 8% annualised volatility target
exit: Closed when implied correlation falls within 2 points of realised correlation, or 15 days before expiry
stop: All positions closed if the VIX closes above 30
marketWatch: The gap between implied and realised correlation among the largest stocks is the main indicator for this strategy now. Scheduled central bank decisions, trade announcements and the peak weeks of earnings season matter because they can either raise correlation or increase differences between stocks. Rehyn also watches how closely the largest technology stocks move together, since their weight in the index affects the correlation priced into options.

favourable.heading: Stocks diverge on company news
favourable.text: Company-specific news favours the strategy because it raises the volatility of individual stocks while the index stays steady. DeepSeek's release in January 2025 moved Nvidia by about 17% in a day while the S&P 500 fell about 1.5%.

favourable.heading: Sector rotation within the index
favourable.text: Rotation between sectors favours the strategy because large moves in opposite directions offset each other at index level. In 2022 energy shares rose while technology shares fell, which supported single-stock volatility more than index volatility.

favourable.heading: Correlation normalises after a shock
favourable.text: Implied correlation that falls back after a shock favours the strategy because the premium earned on index options is restored. After the Covid crash, implied correlation fell through 2021 as company-specific results drove share prices.

adverse.heading: Global sell-offs lift correlation
adverse.text: A global sell-off hurts the strategy because stocks fall together and index volatility rises faster than the volatility of individual stocks. In March 2020 the S&P 500 fell about 12% on 16 March, and almost all of its constituents fell with it.

adverse.heading: Policy shocks hit every sector
adverse.text: Broad policy shocks hurt the strategy because they affect all companies at once, so stock-specific differences matter less. The April 2025 tariff announcement led the S&P 500 to fall about 6% on 4 April, with most sectors falling together.

adverse.heading: Crowded positions unwind together
adverse.text: Crowded positioning hurts the strategy when many funds close dispersion trades at the same time, because they must buy index volatility and sell stock volatility together. Rehyn estimates that this raised losses in the February 2018 volatility spike, when index volatility rose by more than individual stock volatility.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, using index and single-stock option prices and the vega-matched positions above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500, implied volatility and the correlation between stocks, which are then applied to the strategy's index and single-stock options.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find Correlation Premiums?

related.why: Sells index volatility without buying stock volatility. Bears crash risk, losing when volatility rises sharply.
related.cue: Same index leg, no stock hedge

related.why: Buys single-stock volatility before results. Bears premium decay, losing when announcements move shares less than priced.
Trades the price gap between related stocks. Bears the risk that gaps widen, losing when stocks stop moving together.
